criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear mission purpose (reef monitoring: SST, thermal stress, bathymetry, colour-change detection), explicit users (marine/conservation scientists, ground stations) and compelling Australian rationale with data (60%/50% mortality, acidification). Referenced. Lacks quantified mission requirements (resolution, revisit, latency, lifetime) and objective statement.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Gantt chart with weekly columns, task rows, deadlines and per-task descriptions; feasible sequence tied to launch, orbit, ground, comms, EOL. But no contingency allowance, no planned-source list linked to the plan, and internal inconsistency (text says editing in weeks 7–8; chart shows weeks 9–10).

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart. Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Only progress is background reading and completion of four STK tutorials; no design results, calculations or simulation output are presented. The single technical claim made (orbit choice) is incorrect, so it cannot count as evidence of useful design work.

evidence.quote: researched into how coral bleaching occurs and its severity, and also completed STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Logical structure with clear headings, readable professional prose, consistent formatting and a labelled, explained Gantt figure. In-text superscripts match the numbered source list, but sources are bare URLs with no author/title/date, and no reference list in standard format.

evidence.quote: These bleaching events are destructive enough to wipe out entire reefs, displacing billions of animals in the process.

technical_issues.issue: 'geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km' is contradictory: GEO altitude is ~35,786 km; 600 km is LEO and cannot be geostationary or continuously stare at the reef.
End-of-life options include 'leaving it where it is', which conflicts with space-debris mitigation practice; 'graveyard orbit' is inapplicable to the stated altitude.
Claims a further 50% of coral perished in 2017; literature attributes roughly half of shallow-water coral loss to the combined 2016–2017 events.
No quantified mission requirements (ground sample distance, revisit time, data latency, swath, design lifetime) derived from the stated user needs.
Gantt/text contradiction: prose reserves editing for weeks 7–8 while the chart schedules Editing & Finalisation in weeks 9–10.
'30 percent more acidic' should be expressed as pH change (~0.1 unit) or hydrogen-ion increase; the framing is misleading.

overall: Strong, well-referenced mission rationale and a clear Gantt-based plan with appropriate STK software choice, but requirements are unquantified, sources are informal, the orbit statement is technically wrong, and preliminary technical evidence is limited to tutorials.

feedback.summary: You present a clear, well-motivated reef-monitoring mission with explicit users and a strong Australian rationale, supported by a readable Gantt-based plan and a sensible STK software choice. Presentation is clean and professional. To progress, you need quantified mission requirements, a corrected orbit statement (600 km is LEO, not geostationary), fuller source details, contingency planning, and actual preliminary design results rather than tutorial completion alone.
next_steps: Convert your user needs into quantified mission requirements (ground sample distance, revisit time, data latency, swath, design lifetime) and add an explicit objectives statement in the Mission Concept & Rationale section.

Correct the orbit claim in the Project Plan: 600 km is low Earth orbit and cannot be geostationary or provide continuous reef stare; revisit your end-of-life options to align with debris-mitigation practice.

Produce and interpret at least one preliminary technical result (e.g. an STK coverage/revisit or link-budget output) and resolve the Gantt/text editing-week inconsistency, adding contingency allowance and a planned-source list.

criteria.C1: You clearly explain the mission purpose, name the users (marine and conservation scientists, ground stations) and give a compelling Australian rationale with referencing. To reach the top of Accomplished, add quantified requirements (resolution, revisit, latency, lifetime) and an explicit objectives statement. Also correct the 2017 coral-loss claim and reframe '30 percent more acidic' as a pH change (~0.1 unit).
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart has weekly columns, task rows, deadlines and descriptions, and the sequence is feasible and tied to launch, orbit, ground, comms and end-of-life. The next level requires contingency provision, a planned information-source list linked to tasks, and fixing the inconsistency where your text schedules editing in weeks 7–8 but the chart shows weeks 9–10.
criteria.C3: Your reported progress is background reading and completion of STK tutorials 1–4. To move beyond Adequate, present actual preliminary design results, calculations or simulation output with brief interpretation. Note that the orbit claim as written (600 km geostationary) is incorrect, so it cannot yet count as evidence of useful design work.
criteria.C4: Your report is logically structured with clear headings, readable professional prose, consistent formatting and a labelled, explained Gantt figure; superscript citations match your numbered source list. To reach the top of Accomplished, replace bare URLs with full references (author, title, date, source) in a consistent standard format and ensure every in-text citation matches.
